title: Special Districts and the April 2028 ADA Title II Deadline: PDFs | SignalFeed.dev
description: Transit, water, fire, park and library districts have until April 26, 2028 under the ADA Title II web rule. What documents count, the exceptions, where districts stand, and a practical order of work.
h1: Special districts and the April 2028 ADA Title II deadline: what to do about PDFs
body:
Transit agencies, water and sanitation districts, fire districts, park and recreation districts, library districts, ports and other special districts are public entities under Title II of the ADA. The Department of Justice's 2024 web rule (28 CFR part 35, subpart H) gives special district governments until April 26, 2028 to make their web content and mobile apps conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, regardless of population. (The DOJ moved the original dates back by one year in April 2026.)

What counts

The rule covers web content a district provides or makes available, directly or through contractors. For most districts the biggest share of that content is documents: board agendas and packets, minutes, budgets and audits, rate and fee schedules, capital plans, notices of public hearings, permit and service applications, and annual reports. PDFs and Office files posted on the website count, and so do documents a district posts on a separate agenda or document portal.

There are exceptions. The two that matter most for documents are archived web content (created before the compliance date, kept only for reference, research or recordkeeping, not changed after archiving, and stored in a clearly marked archive area) and preexisting conventional electronic documents posted before the compliance date, unless they are currently used to apply for, access or participate in the district's services. A rate application or a current fee schedule is in scope even if it is old. Read the rule's text or ask counsel about edge cases; this page is not legal advice.

Where districts stand

We measured the PDFs on 481 special-district websites reached from the .gov domains registered to special districts. About 40% of the sampled PDFs had no accessibility tags at all, 19% were scanned images with no usable text, and only 2 of 1,439 sampled PDFs passed a veraPDF PDF/UA-1 check. State-by-state numbers are on the special district Backlog Index. These are automated signals, not conformance findings.

A practical order of work

  1. Stop adding to the backlog. Fix the export settings in Word (Save As PDF, Options, "Document structure tags for accessibility") and use heading styles, real lists and table header rows. Our Word-to-PDF guide shows the steps, and the free accessible agenda template handles the most frequent document.
  2. Fix what people use to get service. Applications, forms, current rate and fee schedules, service maps and notices come first.
  3. Decide what is archive. Move true archives to a clearly labelled archive section, and remove documents nobody needs.
  4. Budget the rest. Public contract prices for remediation cluster around $3.50 to $6 per ordinary page; forms, complex layouts and scans cost more. See what PDF remediation costs, and if you need your own numbers for a budget request or RFP, a sizing of your site's PDFs gives the count, page range and per-file detail.
